```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(ggplot2)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
tutorial_options(exercise.timelimit = 30)
```

## Why this tutorial

Team 6's `posterior_plot()` shows a density, the high-density region shaded, markers for mean, median and MAP,
interval bars underneath, and a threshold line. In ggplot2 each of those is a **layer**. This warmup builds that
figure one layer at a time.

About 40 minutes.

## 1. A density curve

We start with draws and a density data frame.

```{r base, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=12}
set.seed(1)
draws <- rbeta(1e4, 2, 12)
d <- density(draws, from = 0, to = 1, n = 512)
dens <- data.frame(x = d$x, y = d$y)

p <- ggplot(dens, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "value", y = "density")
p
```

## 2. Shading a region with `geom_area`

`geom_area()` fills between 0 and `y`. To shade only part of the curve, give the layer its **own data**
(a subset). Shade `x` between 0.02 and 0.30:

```{r shade, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=16}
set.seed(1)
d <- density(rbeta(1e4, 2, 12), from = 0, to = 1, n = 512)
dens <- data.frame(x = d$x, y = d$y)

region <- subset(dens, x >= 0.02 & x <= ______)

ggplot(dens, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_area(data = region, alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line()
```

```{r shade-solution}
set.seed(1)
d <- density(rbeta(1e4, 2, 12), from = 0, to = 1, n = 512)
dens <- data.frame(x = d$x, y = d$y)

region <- subset(dens, x >= 0.02 & x <= 0.30)

ggplot(dens, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_area(data = region, alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line()
```

### Several pieces need a `group`

If the region has two pieces, `geom_area` would join them with a flat strip across the gap. Give each piece
an id and map it to `group`. Run and compare to the version without `group`.

```{r pieces, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=20}
set.seed(3)
d <- density(c(rbeta(5e3, 5, 30), rbeta(5e3, 30, 5)), from = 0, to = 1, n = 512)
dens <- data.frame(x = d$x, y = d$y)
dens$inside <- dens$y > 0.8
dens$piece  <- cumsum(c(TRUE, diff(dens$inside) != 0))
region <- subset(dens, inside)

ggplot(dens, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_area(data = region, aes(group = piece), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line()
```

```{r quiz-group}
quiz(
  question("What does `cumsum(c(TRUE, diff(inside) != 0))` produce?",
    answer("A counter that increases every time `inside` switches between TRUE and FALSE, so each run has its own id.", correct = TRUE),
    answer("The number of TRUE values.", message = "That would be sum(inside)."),
    answer("A logical vector.", message = "cumsum() returns numbers."),
    allow_retry = TRUE)
)
```

## 3. Vertical lines for point estimates

`geom_vline(xintercept = ...)` adds a vertical line. To get **different line types for different estimates and a
legend**, put the values in a data frame and map `linetype` or `colour`.

```{r vline, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=22}
set.seed(1)
draws <- rbeta(1e4, 2, 12)
d <- density(draws, from = 0, to = 1, n = 512)
dens <- data.frame(x = d$x, y = d$y)

pts <- data.frame(
  estimate = c("mean", "median", "MAP"),
  value    = c(mean(draws), median(draws), dens$x[which.max(dens$y)]))

ggplot(dens, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(data = pts, aes(xintercept = value, linetype = estimate), colour = "grey30") +
  labs(x = "value", y = "density", linetype = NULL)
```

## 4. Interval bars below the curve

An interval is a horizontal segment: `geom_segment()` with `x`, `xend`, `y`, `yend`. We place the bars just below
zero by using negative `y` values. Because the layer's data (`bars`) has no column called `y` in the base plot's
aesthetics, set `inherit.aes = FALSE` so the layer doesn't look for the base plot's `aes(x, y)`.

```{r bars, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=22}
set.seed(1)
draws <- rbeta(1e4, 2, 12)
d <- density(draws, from = 0, to = 1, n = 512)
dens <- data.frame(x = d$x, y = d$y)
ymax <- max(dens$y)

bars <- data.frame(
  type  = c("ETI", "HDI"),
  lower = c(0.019, 0.005),
  upper = c(0.360, 0.319),
  y     = c(-0.04, -0.08) * ymax)

ggplot(dens, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_segment(data = bars, aes(x = lower, xend = upper, y = y, yend = y, colour = type),
               linewidth = 2, inherit.aes = ______)
```

```{r bars-hint-1}
# TRUE would try to use aes(x, y) from the base plot; we want FALSE
```

```{r bars-solution}
set.seed(1)
draws <- rbeta(1e4, 2, 12)
d <- density(draws, from = 0, to = 1, n = 512)
dens <- data.frame(x = d$x, y = d$y)
ymax <- max(dens$y)

bars <- data.frame(
  type  = c("ETI", "HDI"),
  lower = c(0.019, 0.005),
  upper = c(0.360, 0.319),
  y     = c(-0.04, -0.08) * ymax)

ggplot(dens, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_segment(data = bars, aes(x = lower, xend = upper, y = y, yend = y, colour = type),
               linewidth = 2, inherit.aes = FALSE)
```

## 5. Threshold line and a text label

`annotate("text", x, y, label)` draws one label without needing a data frame. Add a dashed threshold line at
0.2 and label it with the probability above it.

```{r thresh, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=18}
set.seed(1)
draws <- rbeta(1e4, 2, 12)
d <- density(draws, from = 0, to = 1, n = 512)
dens <- data.frame(x = d$x, y = d$y)
thr <- 0.2
pr <- mean(draws > thr)

ggplot(dens, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = thr, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = thr, y = max(dens$y),
           label = paste0("P(> ", thr, ") = ", round(pr, 3)), hjust = -0.05)
```

```{r quiz-layers}
quiz(
  question("A package test can check a plot by looking at the class of each layer's geom, e.g. `class(p$layers[[1]]$geom)`. Such a test of \"has an area layer\" passes if the plot:",
    answer("contains a `geom_area()` layer somewhere.", correct = TRUE),
    answer("has the word 'area' in its title.", message = "Titles are not layers."),
    answer("is drawn with shading, however it was produced.", message = "The test inspects the layers, not the pixels."),
    allow_retry = TRUE)
)
```

### Where this leads

Team 6's `posterior_plot()` stacks these layers: HPD area (with `group` for pieces), vertical lines for mean,
median and MAP, interval bars at negative `y`, and an optional threshold line with an `annotate()` label. The tests
look at which layers are present, so build in layers rather than as one picture.
